tasks.gr11-momentum-t2: Topic: Momentum and Impulse. Cover momentum as a vector (p = mv, SI unit: kg·m/s), impulse (J = FΔt = Δp), the impulse-momentum theorem, the law of conservation of momentum for isolated systems (Σp_before = Σp_after), elastic collisions (KE conserved), inelastic collisions (KE not conserved), and perfectly inelastic collisions (objects stick together). Ask Grade 11 learners to calculate momentum and impulse, apply conservation of momentum to one-dimensional collisions, classify collision types, and interpret force-time graphs for impulse.
tasks.gr11-projectile-motion-t2: Topic: Vertical Projectile Motion. Cover free-fall under gravity (g = 9.8 m/s² downward), the kinematic equations for vertical projectiles (v = v_i + gΔt, Δy = v_i Δt + ½gΔt², v² = v_i² + 2gΔy), upward-launched projectiles (maximum height where v = 0, symmetry of flight), downward projectiles, and qualitative effect of air resistance. Ask Grade 11 learners to calculate time of flight, maximum height, and velocity at any point for both upward and downward projectiles; interpret velocity-time graphs; and apply kinematic equations systematically.
tasks.gr11-electrostatics-t2: Topic: Electrostatics. Cover types of electric charge (positive and negative), conservation of charge, Coulomb's law (F = kQ₁Q₂/r², k = 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²), the electric field (E = F/q = kQ/r²), electric field lines (direction from positive to negative, density indicates field strength, lines never cross), and superposition of fields. Ask Grade 11 learners to calculate electrostatic forces and field strengths, determine net force or field from multiple charges, sketch electric field patterns, and apply Coulomb's law to charge and distance problems.
tasks.gr11-electric-circuits-t2: Topic: Electric Circuits. Cover conventional current (I = Q/Δt), potential difference (V), resistance, Ohm's law (V = IR), series circuits (same current everywhere, V_total = ΣV_i, R_total = ΣR_i), parallel circuits (same voltage across branches, I_total = ΣI_i, 1/R_total = Σ1/R_i), emf and internal resistance (ε = V_terminal + Ir), and power dissipation (P = VI = I²R = V²/R). Ask Grade 11 learners to analyse series and parallel circuits, calculate equivalent resistance, determine terminal voltage under load, and solve power problems in multi-component circuits.
